title: Rotate credentials already exposed through MCP tool results and dry-run output
description: Identify credentials that the pre-fix mongodb-mcp-server may already have exposed. (a) Atlas DB users created by atlas-create-db-user with an auto-generated password: list them from the Atlas project audit log or database users list, created before task 1's deployment, and reset their passwords through Secrets Manager. (b) Any run of MDB_MCP_DRY_RUN / --dryRun in dev, qa or prod: search container stdout and Wazuh logs (prod retention 365 days) for the dry-run config dump. For each hit, rotate the MCP connection string credentials, Atlas apiClientSecret and voyageApiKey, and purge or restrict the log entries under the log-retention owner's approval. Do not copy any found secret into tickets, task evidence or this workspace; record only locators and timestamps. Constraints: rotate prod credentials in a coordinated window with the mcp-gateway operators because a rotated connection string needs a redeploy (releaseProcess dev -> qa -> prod, 1 approval).
acceptanceCriteria: A Wazuh/container-log search for the dry-run dump signature (e.g. the apiClientSecret key name in a JSON config block) across dev, qa and prod is recorded with its query, time range and hit count
Every Atlas DB user created with an auto-generated password before task 1 was deployed has a password reset timestamp later than that deployment

For every environment with a dry-run hit, the connection string credentials, apiClientSecret and voyageApiKey show a rotation timestamp in Secrets Manager or Atlas, and the server passes a post-rotation health check

verificationMethod.description: CISO reviews the recorded log-search queries and hit counts, the Atlas database user password-reset list, and Secrets Manager rotation timestamps (locators only), all attached as task evidence. Expected result: every exposed credential is rotated after the fixes from tasks 1 and 2 were deployed, and no secret value appears in the evidence.

rootCause.description: Before the fix, generated passwords reached MCP client transcripts and unredacted config reached stdout/container logs, so credentials issued before the code change must be treated as disclosed.
